summary: LMCache: 16-bit multimodal hash collision can poison KV cache entries
details:
LMCache's vLLM multimodal integration reduced each multimodal item identifier (image hash or request-scoped identifier) to a 16-bit value via `hex_hash_to_int16()` in `lmcache/integration/vllm/utils.py`, and filled the whole placeholder span with that single value before token-based chunk hashing. With only 65,536 possible values, distinct images with the same placeholder layout and surrounding prompt could produce identical KV cache keys (birthday bound: ~50% collision probability at ~300 distinct images), causing LMCache to return KV cache entries computed for a different image. This can produce incorrect model output and may expose visual context across requests or users.

The issue was fixed in LMCache 0.5.5 by LMCache/LMCache#4783, which removes the 16-bit truncation and fills each placeholder position with a distinct 31-bit value derived from the full identifier (SHA-256), so cache keys carry the full multimodal identity.

### Workarounds
Upgrade to 0.5.5 or later. If upgrading is not possible, disable LMCache for multimodal requests.
